title: Smallest Number With All Set Bits
statement: For a positive integer `n`, find the smallest integer `x` with `x >= n` whose binary form is made of `1` digits only, with no `0` anywhere, and return it.
notes:
## Intuition

The numbers written with ones only are `1, 3, 7, 15, 31, ...`: each is one less than a power of two, `2^b - 1` for `b` ones. If `n` has `b` binary digits, then `2^b - 1` has the same length with every digit set, so it is at least `n`. Any all-ones number with fewer digits is at most `2^(b-1) - 1`, which is below `n` because `n`'s top digit alone is worth `2^(b-1)`. So the answer is `2^b - 1`: the power of two just above `n`, minus one.

Counting up from `n` and testing each binary string also works, but it inspects up to `n` numbers instead of `log n` bits.

## Approach

1. Count the binary digits of `n`: shift a copy, `rest`, right by one until it reaches `0`, adding one to `bits` each time.
2. `1 << bits` is a `1` followed by `bits` zeros, the power of two just above `n`. Subtracting one turns it into `bits` ones; return that.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 5` is `101` in binary. `rest` goes `5 → 2 → 1 → 0`, so `bits = 3`. Then `(1 << 3) - 1 = 8 - 1 = 7`, which is `111`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(log n): one loop step per binary digit of `n`.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- `n` may already be all ones (Example 3, `n = 3`): the answer is `n` itself, and the method gives it because `bits = 2` and `2^2 - 1 = 3`.
- Use the power of two strictly above `n`. For `n = 4` (`100`) that is `8`, giving `7`; rounding `n` up to a power of two (`4` itself) would give `3`, which is smaller than `n`.
- `1 << 31` overflows a 32-bit integer in Java or C; here `bits` is at most `10`, so it is safe.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `bits` | number of binary digits of `n` counted so far |
| `rest` | what is left of `n` after the digits already counted are shifted out |

narration.2: No binary digits of n have been counted yet.
narration.3: Work on a copy of n so its digits can be shifted away one at a time.
narration.4: While any set bit is left, n has at least one more binary digit.
narration.6: Shift right by one to drop the lowest digit.
narration.8: 1 << bits is the power of two just above n; one less is bits ones in a row, the smallest such number that is at least n.
